artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $r \geq 1$ be an integer, and let $z_1, \dots, z_r$ be complex numbers on the unit circle (so $|z_1| = \cdots = |z_r| = 1$). Let $p_1, \dots, p_r$ be nonnegative real weights satisfying the normalization
$$p_1 + p_2 + \cdots + p_r = r.$$
Prove or disprove the following assertion: for every such choice of points $\{z_j\}$ and weights $\{p_j\}$, there exists a complex number $z$ with $|z|=1$ such that
$$\prod_{j=1}^{r} |z - z_j|^{\,p_j} \;\geq\; 2.$$
(The constant $2$ on the right-hand side is best possible, as seen by taking $r=1$, $p_1=1$, and any $z_1$ on the unit circle.) Equivalently, show that the Chebyshev-type extremal quantity
$$\sup_{|z|=1} \prod_{j=1}^{r} |z - z_j|^{p_j}$$
is at least $2$ for all admissible configurations $(z_j, p_j)$.
artifact.category_tag: Weighted Chebyshev constants on the unit circle
artifact.status_search_result: The equal-weight version (a conjecture of Ambrus, Ball, and Erdélyi) and the equally-spaced-points case are known, and the general weighted polarization-type conjecture on the unit circle has been studied (e.g. Hardin–Kendall–Saff, Ambrus–Ball). However, web searches did not produce a definitive proof or disproof of the general weighted product inequality with arbitrary nonnegative weights summing to $r$, so the present status is not conclusively established by the sources retrieved.

status_evidence.title: Chebyshev constants for the unit circle (Ambrus, Ball, Erdélyi)
status_evidence.snippet: Studies the extremal problem of maximizing products of distances on the unit circle and resolves several special cases (equal weights, equally spaced points).
status_evidence.claim: Special cases of the conjecture are established.

status_evidence.title: Polarization optimality of equally spaced points on the circle for discrete potentials
status_evidence.snippet: Hardin, Kendall, and Saff prove optimality of equally spaced points for a class of discrete potentials on the circle, addressing the Ambrus–Ball–Erdélyi conjecture.
status_evidence.claim: Equal-weight / equally spaced cases are resolved, but the weighted product form is not fully addressed.
